slot.brief: Give the observed molar mass of a complex salt in solution (or its measured boiling point elevation) and ask to deduce the dissociation/association and hence the number of ions or the formula of the complex.

stem: A $0.10\ \text{m}$ aqueous solution of $\text{CoCl}_3\cdot n\text{NH}_3$ boils at $100.156^\circ\text{C}$. Assuming complete ionization, the formula of the complex is ($K_b\text{ for water} = 0.52\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$):

verdicts.working: ΔTb = 100.156 − 100 = 0.156 K. i = ΔTb/(Kb·m) = 0.156/(0.52×0.10) = 3. Complete ionization must give 3 ions per formula unit: [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 → [Co(NH3)5Cl]²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ (3 ions). A gives 1, B gives 2, D gives 4.

working:
1. Calculate the boiling point elevation:
$$\Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^\circ = 100.156^\circ\text{C} - 100.000^\circ\text{C} = 0.156\ \text{K}$$

2. Use the relation $\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m$ to determine the van 't Hoff factor $i$:
$$0.156 = i \times 0.52 \times 0.10$$
$$0.156 = i \times 0.052 \implies i = \dfrac{0.156}{0.052} = 3$$

3. Relate $i$ to the dissociation of the complex:
For $100\%$ ionization, $i$ equals the total number of ions produced per formula unit.
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$ is a non-electrolyte ($i = 1$).
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl} \rightarrow [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+ + \text{Cl}^-$ ($2$ ions, $i = 2$).
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^-$ ($3$ ions, $i = 3$).
- $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^-$ ($4$ ions, $i = 4$).

Therefore, the complex is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$.

Independent check: ΔTb = 100.156 − 100 = 0.156 K. i = ΔTb/(Kb·m) = 0.156/(0.52×0.10) = 3. Complete ionization must give 3 ions per formula unit: [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 → [Co(NH3)5Cl]²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ (3 ions). A gives 1, B gives 2, D gives 4.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A encodes neglecting the van 't Hoff factor entirely (taking $i = 1$, non-electrolyte).
Option B encodes an arithmetic slip in evaluating $i = \Delta T_b / (K_b m)$ to give $i = 2$.
Option D encodes the common misconception of confusing the total number of ions ($i = 3$) with the number of ionizable chloride counter-ions outside the coordination sphere.
